question: Ticket b03dce633aa8 says 'D3 has code (number_open) surgically update the _NEXT digits in 0.6 after minting each Q#', but outline 0.10 reads "An artifact is present tense or past tense, never both. Present tense is rewritten whole and points at its provenance; past tense is append-only, opened when needed, and read cold only through a compiled face (state, the latest slate). WHY: what a cold reader loads at an address should be what is true now." (0.10 specifies that present-tense artifacts are 'rewritten whole' — not surgically edited by code. The outline file is present-tense, so updates should involve whole-section rewrites reflecting current design thinking, not programmatic field updates. This blurs the boundary 0.9 established between outline (design) and code (implementation).). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
